findings.quote: and to take responsibility for everything, since we will do what is ordered
findings.problem: πᾶν ἀναδέχεσθαι διότι ποιήσομεν τὸ προσταττόμενον: διότι here means 'that' (content clause after ἀναδέχεσθαι, 'guarantee that'), not causal 'since'.
findings.proposed_fix: and to guarantee that we will do everything that is ordered

findings.quote: Hasdrubal said that he did not understand him.
findings.problem: ὁ δ᾽ Ἀσδρούβας ἀγνοεῖν αὐτὸν ἔφη: Hasdrubal said that Gulussa (αὐτόν, subject of ἀγνοεῖν) was mistaken / did not know the situation; the following καὶ γάρ explains what Gulussa does not know. The English reverses who is ignorant.
findings.proposed_fix: Hasdrubal said that Gulussa was mistaken.

findings.quote: or the troops outside the walls, saying that they were safe;
findings.problem: οὐ γάρ πω … ἠκηκόει … τὰ περὶ τῶν ὑπαίθρων δυνάμεων [ὅτι σώζονται]: this is the narrator's aside (he had not yet heard the news about the forces in the field); ὅτι σώζονται is bracketed as suspect by the editor and in any case is not something Hasdrubal 'says'. The English attributes a doubtful phrase to Hasdrubal's speech.
findings.proposed_fix: or the forces in the field;

findings.quote: For they would not, he said, allow themselves to be seen openly violating a truce, but would give many opportunities for salvation.
findings.problem: οὐ γὰρ περιόψεσθαι σφᾶς προφανῶς παρασπονδουμένους: the gods would not stand by and watch them (the Carthaginians, σφᾶς) being openly wronged in breach of the treaty. The English inverts it, making the gods the would-be treaty-breakers.
findings.proposed_fix: For the gods, he said, would not stand by and see them so openly wronged in breach of the treaty, but would give them many opportunities for salvation.

findings.quote: that among the Greeks and among the Carthaginians of that time one would not easily find two men more alike as masters of affairs
findings.problem: προστάτας πραγμάτων ὁμοιοτέρους τῶν παρὰ τοῖς Ἕλλησι τότε καὶ παρὰ τοῖς Καρχηδονίοις ὑπαρξάντων οὐκ ἂν εὕροι τις ῥᾳδίως: genitive of comparison — one would not easily find leaders more alike than those the Greeks and Carthaginians had at that time. Plural leaders, not 'two men', and not a search 'among' them.
findings.proposed_fix: that one would not easily find leaders of affairs more alike than those who led the Greeks and the Carthaginians at that time

units.note: Stray closing quotation mark at end of chapter ("side by side.”") is outside the error classes; not proposed.

findings.quote: When the envoys who had come from the Peloponnese to Aurelius arrived
findings.problem: παραγενομένων ἐκ Πελοποννήσου τῶν περὶ τὸν Αὐρήλιον πρεσβευτῶν: the envoys are Aurelius and his colleagues, returning from the Peloponnese to Rome; they were not sent 'to Aurelius'.
findings.proposed_fix: When Aurelius and his fellow envoys arrived from the Peloponnese

findings.quote: assumed that the Romans were acting with hypocrisy because the war in Carthage was still unfinished
findings.problem: ὑπελάμβανον καθ᾽ ὑπόκρισιν τοὺς Ῥωμαίους *** διὰ τὸ μένειν ἀτελῆ τὰ κατὰ Καρχηδόνα: the Greek has a lacuna where the verb of the infinitive clause stood; the English supplies 'were acting' as if the text were whole.
findings.proposed_fix: assumed that the Romans [...] by way of pretense, because the war against Carthage was still unfinished

units.note: Lacuna in 38.9: the missing verb cannot be recovered; mark the gap.

findings.quote: the justice of what the envoys from Sextus were saying
findings.problem: τοῖς ὑπὸ τῶν περὶ τὸν Σέξτον λεγομένοις δικαίοις: Sextus and his colleagues are themselves the Roman envoys; not 'envoys from Sextus'.
findings.proposed_fix: the justice of what Sextus and his colleagues were saying

findings.quote: men who had been deliberately selected as the worst from every city
findings.problem: οὗτοι δ᾽ ἦσαν ὥσπερ ἐπίτηδες ἐξ ἑκάστης πόλεως κατ᾽ ἐκλογὴν οἱ χείριστοι: ὥσπερ ('as if') makes it a comparison — they were the worst of each city, as though picked on purpose; the English states as fact that they were deliberately selected.
findings.proposed_fix: men who were the worst of every city, as if picked out on purpose

findings.quote: and there confer with the Lacedaemonians so that some agreed settlement
findings.problem: κοινολογηθέντες τοῖς Λακεδαιμονίοις ***, ἵνα γένηταί τις ὡμολογημένη λύσις: lacuna after Λακεδαιμονίοις (the main verb of the reported reply is lost); the English reads on as if whole.
findings.proposed_fix: and there confer with the Lacedaemonians [...] so that some agreed settlement

units.note: Lacuna in 38.10 after Λακεδαιμονίοις; mark, do not supply.
